csKnowledge: staged pipeline / cascade composition with per-stage gating
pass1.buildNote: Each cascade stage must gate the next on a real confidence threshold — never blend two enhancement passes into one double-applied result.

pass2.systemImpact: The feature cascade feeds aiReasoningDispatcher and is consumed by AICapabilityMaximizerEngine's recommendation path; a regression here double-applies an enhancement pass so downstream AI-WIRE-MS0 round-trip E2Es and ai-feature-recommend hook injections surface inflated or contradictory scores. AWARE-MS0::U-AWARE06 (feature recommendation injection) depends on a stable cascade ordering.
csDepth: Per-stage gating on a confidence threshold introduces a short-circuit branch — verify the cascade is idempotent under re-entry (a memoized stage must key on the full input hash, not a partial), or a stale memo silently skips a needed recompute.

Feature-importance re-ranking after each stage is O(n log n) per stage and O(stages·n log n) overall; if stage count grows the re-rank dominates — consider an incremental heap update instead of a full sort.

pass1.buildNote: Skill commands are thin routers — keep logic in the dispatcher action, and validate command frontmatter against command-frontmatter.schema.json.

pass2.systemImpact: These skill commands are thin routers into aiReasoningDispatcher actions; if their frontmatter drifts from command-frontmatter.schema.json the skill-auto-loader and skill-auto-trigger hooks silently fail to surface them, so the reasoning capability becomes unreachable from the prompt surface even though the dispatcher action still works. Slash-command fidelity tests gate this.
csDepth: Reasoning-chain DAG traversal must detect cycles — a self-referential reasoning chain causes unbounded recursion; use an explicit visited-set with depth cap rather than relying on natural termination.
The command-to-dispatcher routing table is a hot lookup; a hash map keyed by command name is correct, but keep logic out of the command (R5 — code answers deterministic routing, not the model).

pass1.buildNote: A protective hook must exit 0 and signal block via stdout JSON only — exit-2 silently truncates on Windows pipes and bypasses the gate.

pass2.systemImpact: A protective PreToolUse hook sits in the fleet-wide hook chain ahead of the first tool call; if it throws or mis-blocks it stalls every chat, and if it silently passes a bad payload it lets a degraded AI-capability state propagate into AI-MAX-MS0 builds. It must be wired in settings.json (an on-disk-only hook never fires) and respect MINIMAL_ALLOWLIST so a hook profile cannot disable it.
csDepth: The exit-2 pipe-truncation hazard is Windows-specific: a non-zero exit closes the stdout pipe before the JSON block flushes, so the gate is silently bypassed — always exit 0 and signal block via stdout JSON.
Hook latency is on the critical path of every tool call; bound any file read (size cap before JSON.parse) and avoid synchronous network calls — a slow guard hook degrades the whole fleet.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-ACADEMY.title: Train CrossDisciplinaryDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with train/validation split
feature extraction from a heterogeneous corpus (CAD + course + kernel)
checkpoint serialization with embedded training metadata

pass2.systemImpact: CrossDisciplinaryDeepLearningEngine is PRISM's cross-domain synthesis entry point (15 scientific domains); a checkpoint that overfits the JM-DIE corpus poisons every consumer of prismCreativeReasoningEngine and the recommendAIFeatures path. Per the pre-revenue doctrine, all revenue milestones are gated behind this training pass landing correctly.
csDepth: A heterogeneous corpus (CAD + course + kernel) needs per-source feature normalization before the train/validation split — splitting raw then normalizing leaks validation statistics into training (the NN-GRAPH stratified-negative lesson).

Checkpoint serialization must embed training metadata (corpus fingerprint, split seed, epoch) so the U2 self-retrain lifecycle can decide promote/decline deterministically; an undated checkpoint cannot be drift-compared.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-ACADEMY.title: Train MITCourseDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: Probe the course-corpus JSON schema before ingesting — assuming a shape without reading the file is the recurring schema-blindness bug.

pass2.systemImpact: MITCourseDeepLearningEngine feeds the course-content-to-KnowledgeTip routing that the cad-engine knowledge_store auto-loads; a bad checkpoint degrades tribal-tip recommendations across /pdf-learn and /video-learn outputs. Probe the course-corpus JSON schemaVersion before ingest — the recurring schema-blindness bug is assuming totals.* vs top-level field placement without reading the file.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-CAM-CAM.title: Train CAMDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with train/validation split
k-NN / similarity index over training examples
pass1.buildNote: Hold out a validation slice from the 76K JM-DIE corpus and assert real accuracy before promoting — never train and evaluate on the same data.

pass2.systemImpact: CAMDeepLearningEngine's strategy predictions are consumed by camDispatcher toolpath selection; a checkpoint that memorizes JM-DIE answers ships wrong CAM strategy recommendations into the print-to-program pipeline, breaking DOMAIN-PIPELINE-MS0's TOOLPATH_GEN stage. The CAM orchestrator unit (sibling) wraps this engine.
csDepth: A k-NN similarity index over training examples is O(n) per query without an ANN structure — for a 76K corpus build a ball-tree / HNSW index or queries dominate inference latency.
CAM toolpath feature vectorization must be order-invariant where toolpath operations commute; encoding operation order into the vector causes the model to learn a spurious sequencing signal.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-CAM-CAM.title: Train CAMDeepLearningOrchestratorEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: orchestration of multiple sub-model training stages
supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: An orchestrator must fail loud if any wrapped CAM deep-learning engine is missing — never silently skip a sub-model and report success.

pass2.systemImpact: The CAM orchestrator ensembles per-engine CAM deep-learning predictions; if a wrapped engine is missing it must fail loud, not silently drop a sub-model — a silent skip degrades the ensemble's accuracy invisibly and the DOMAIN-PIPELINE-MS0 orchestrator stage that depends on it ships wrong toolpaths with full confidence.
csDepth: Ensemble aggregation must define a tie/abstain policy — if sub-models disagree at equal weight, returning an arbitrary winner hides genuine uncertainty; surface it (R12).

Orchestrating multiple training stages introduces a partial-failure mode: a crash on stage 3 of 5 leaves stages 1-2 checkpoints written — make stage writes atomic and resumable, not all-or-nothing in memory.

The cad-fusion-training-ms0 wiki records that Fusion cloud is unreachable without Forge creds, so the corpus pivots to Inventor/STEP — this unit must use that same transferable B-rep corpus.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-CAM-HYP.title: Train HyperMillDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: HyperMillDeepLearningEngine is a ghost engine — build then train; assert real accuracy on held-out hyperMILL programs.

pass2.systemImpact: HyperMillDeepLearningEngine (ghost) once built feeds hyperMILL strategy selection through camDispatcher and the hyperMILL automation bridge (CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT07). hyperMILL has 25 already-extracted assets — do not re-extract; the model should consume the existing function index.
csDepth: hyperMILL strategy feature vectorization shares structure with the generic CAM engine — extract a shared vectorizer to avoid two divergent feature spaces that the orchestrator cannot ensemble.
k-NN over a sparse strategy space risks empty neighborhoods for rare strategies; fall back to a class-prior rather than returning a nearest-but-irrelevant match.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-CAM-MAS.title: Train MastercamDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: MastercamDeepLearningEngine is a ghost engine — build it, then train on JM-DIE Mastercam programs; verify strategy-prediction accuracy on a held-out set.

pass2.systemImpact: MastercamDeepLearningEngine (ghost) feeds Mastercam strategy selection consumed by camDispatcher and MastercamMultiAxisEngine. Mastercam has 45 already-extracted assets — the model trains on those, not a re-extraction. A bad checkpoint mis-routes the most-used CAM vendor's strategy.
csDepth: Softmax classification over strategy classes needs class-balanced sampling — a JM-DIE corpus heavily skewed toward a few strategies trains a model that always predicts the majority class with high softmax confidence.
Validate prediction accuracy with a stratified held-out set so each strategy class is represented in evaluation, not just the common ones.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-DATABAS.title: Train ToolDatabaseDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
similarity search over the tool catalog
pass1.buildNote: ToolDatabaseDeepLearningEngine is a ghost engine — build it, train on the tool catalog, and validate recommendations against held-out tool usage.

pass2.systemImpact: ToolDatabaseDeepLearningEngine (ghost) once built recommends tools consumed by speed/feed and CAM toolpath units; a checkpoint that overfits poisons tool selection across the print-to-program TOOLING_SELECT stage. The tool catalog is the ground-truth source — schema-probe it before embedding.
csDepth: Tool-record embedding must handle mixed categorical (material, coating) and continuous (diameter, flute count) features — one-hot the categoricals or the model treats nominal codes as ordinal.
Similarity search over the tool catalog is a nearest-neighbor query; for an updatable catalog choose an index that supports incremental insert, or every catalog update forces a full rebuild.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-LATHE-L.title: Train LatheDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with train/validation split
pass1.buildNote: Train LatheDeepLearningEngine on a held-out validation slice of the lathe archive — assert real prediction accuracy before promoting the checkpoint.

pass2.systemImpact: LatheDeepLearningEngine feeds turningDispatcher and the lathe studio pipeline; a regression mis-predicts lathe program parameters consumed by DOMAIN-PIPELINE-MS0's lathe FULL_PIPELINE. LatheDeepReasoningEngine (sibling) shares the lathe corpus, so feature-space agreement matters.
csDepth: Lathe-program feature extraction must canonicalize G-code dialect first (Okuma S[Vnn] vs Fanuc S-numeric) — the regex trap documented in PRISM regressions causes the model to learn dialect noise as signal.
Train/validation split should be by program (not by line) so a held-out program is wholly unseen — line-level splitting leaks the same program's structure into both sets.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-LATHE-L.title: Train LatheDeepLearningIntelligenceEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: LatheDeepLearningIntelligenceEngine is a ghost engine — build then train; verify generalization on held-out lathe programs.

pass2.systemImpact: LatheDeepLearningIntelligenceEngine (ghost) once built layers reasoning-chain inference over LatheDeepReasoningEngine; it is consumed by the lathe AGI master path. A ghost-build must dedup-check first — the intelligence-tier engine may overlap an existing reasoning engine.
csDepth: Reasoning-chain feature vectorization over variable-length chains needs a fixed-dimension encoding (pooling or attention) — padding to a max length wastes capacity and biases toward short chains.
k-NN similarity over training examples must define a distance metric appropriate to the embedding space — cosine for normalized embeddings, not Euclidean, or magnitude dominates.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-LATHE-L.title: Train LatheKinematicsDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: Kinematics labels must come from canonical FK/IK math — never let the model invent kinematics; validate against analytically-computed ground truth.

pass2.systemImpact: LatheKinematicsDeepLearningEngine predictions feed the lathe kinematic-validity path; if the model invents kinematics rather than deferring to canonical FK/IK math, downstream collision and work-envelope checks accept physically impossible programs. Kinematics labels are safety-relevant ground truth.
csDepth: Forward/inverse kinematics ground-truth labelling must come from the deterministic InverseKinematicsSolverEngine — never let the trained model become the authority on kinematics; it is an accelerator over math, not a replacement.
IK can have multiple valid solutions (elbow-up/elbow-down); the labelling must pick a canonical branch consistently or the model trains on contradictory labels for identical inputs.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-LATHE-L.title: Train LatheMetaLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

pass1.buildNote: Meta-learning needs a distribution of tasks, not one dataset — partition the lathe corpus into distinct tasks and validate fast-adaptation on unseen tasks.

pass2.systemImpact: LatheMetaLearningEngine produces fast-adapting models for new lathe tasks; its meta-learned initialization feeds LatheDeepLearningEngine fine-tuning. If the task partition is wrong it learns a single-task model masquerading as a meta-learner — every downstream fast-adapt claim is then false.
csDepth: Meta-learning needs a distribution of tasks — partition the lathe corpus by material/operation/machine into distinct tasks; treating one dataset as one task collapses MAML to ordinary training.
MAML's inner/outer loop is second-order (gradient through a gradient); first-order approximation (FOMAML) is cheaper — choose explicitly and document the accuracy/cost tradeoff.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-LATHE-L.title: Train LatheSpeedFeedDeepLearningAdvisorEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

pass1.buildNote: Speed/feed predictions must stay bounded by canonical Kienzle/Taylor physics — never inline constants; cross-check ML output against the physics envelope.

pass2.systemImpact: LatheSpeedFeedDeepLearningAdvisorEngine output feeds the lathe speed/feed advisory consumed by /auto-speed-feed-lathe and the SPEED_FEED pipeline stage; an ML prediction outside the Kienzle/Taylor physics envelope produces unsafe spindle/feed values that the SAFETY_VALIDATE stage must catch — but the advisor must self-clamp first.
csDepth: ML speed/feed output must be clamped to the canonical physics envelope post-prediction — the model is an interpolator within the safe region, never an extrapolator past it.
Speed/feed is a regression target with heteroscedastic noise (variance grows with cut depth) — a plain MSE loss underweights high-DOC error; consider a relative or quantile loss.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-FI.title: Train FiveAxisAIUltraIntelligenceEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: FiveAxisAIUltraIntelligenceEngine is a ghost engine — build it; collision-avoidance predictions must defer to the deterministic collision engine, never override it.

pass2.systemImpact: FiveAxisAIUltraIntelligenceEngine (ghost) once built feeds 5-axis tilt/collision advisory; its collision-avoidance predictions must DEFER to the deterministic collision engine, never override it — a model that overrides a deterministic safety check ships a crash. fiveAxisDispatcher consumers depend on this hierarchy.
csDepth: Collision-avoidance is a hard safety constraint, not a learned objective — the ML layer proposes tilt candidates, the deterministic WorkEnvelopeValidatorEngine vetoes; this two-tier design must be enforced structurally, not by convention.
5-axis collision feature representation is high-dimensional (tool + part + fixture geometry); dimensionality reduction risks discarding the exact feature that distinguishes a near-miss from a crash.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-FI.title: Train FiveAxisDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: FiveAxisDeepLearningEngine is a ghost engine — build then train; validate on held-out 5-axis programs and keep collision logic deterministic.

pass2.systemImpact: FiveAxisDeepLearningEngine (ghost) feeds 5-axis toolpath optimization through fiveAxisDispatcher; collision logic must stay deterministic — the model optimizes within the validated region only. Downstream the FiveAxis ultra-intelligence engine (sibling) ensembles this.
csDepth: 5-axis toolpath feature vectorization must encode the rotary-axis pair correctly (the rotation_order 2-char rotary-pair convention from PRISM regressions) — mislabeling A/B/C pairs trains the model on inconsistent kinematics.
Validation on held-out 5-axis programs must check no predicted toolpath enters a collision state — accuracy alone is insufficient for a safety-adjacent model.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-MI.title: Train MillDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with train/validation split
pass1.buildNote: MillDeepLearningEngine is a ghost engine — build then train on the 76K corpus; assert real accuracy on a held-out mill-program slice.

pass2.systemImpact: MillDeepLearningEngine (ghost) feeds milling program prediction through millDispatcher and the mill studio; a ghost-build must dedup-check against MillingDeepReasoningEngine and MillingDeepIntegrationEngine first — the milling domain has dense engine coverage. DOMAIN-PIPELINE-MS0's mill FULL_PIPELINE consumes it.
csDepth: Milling-program feature extraction over a 76K corpus is the memory bottleneck — stream the corpus and accumulate features incrementally rather than loading all programs into memory.
Train/validation split by program with a fixed seed makes the regression oracle reproducible; an unseeded split makes accuracy non-comparable across runs.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-MI.title: Train MillingAIUltraIntelligenceEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: MillingAIUltraIntelligenceEngine is a ghost engine — build it; if using LoRA adapters, verify rank allocation and validate on held-out tasks.

pass2.systemImpact: MillingAIUltraIntelligenceEngine (ghost) is the top-tier milling intelligence consumed by the milling AGI master path; if it uses LoRA adapters, the AdaLoRARankAllocatorEngine and FederatedLoRAEngine govern rank — a mis-sized adapter underfits or wastes capacity, degrading every milling reasoning consumer.
csDepth: LoRA rank allocation is a capacity/cost tradeoff — too low underfits the milling-strategy manifold, too high erases the parameter-efficiency benefit; let AdaLoRARankAllocatorEngine decide rather than hardcoding rank.
Knowledge synthesis / ensemble fusion across sub-models needs a fusion weight that is itself validated — uniform averaging assumes equal sub-model competence, which is rarely true.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-MI.title: Train MillingMetaLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

pass1.buildNote: Partition the milling corpus into distinct tasks for the meta-learner — validate fast-adaptation on tasks held out of the meta-training set.

pass2.systemImpact: MillingMetaLearningEngine produces fast-adapting milling models; its meta-learned init feeds MillDeepLearningEngine fine-tuning and is referenced by the milling tribal-corpus bridge. A bad task partition collapses the meta-learner to single-task training, invalidating all fast-adapt claims downstream.
csDepth: Partition the milling corpus into distinct tasks (by material/feature/machine) — the meta-learner's value is fast adaptation to an UNSEEN task, so the held-out validation tasks must not overlap meta-training tasks.
MAML inner/outer loop second-order gradients are memory-heavy on a large corpus — batch task sampling and consider FOMAML to bound memory.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-VI.title: Train VirtualMachiningDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: VirtualMachiningDeepLearningEngine is a ghost engine — build then train; validate simulated predictions against real machining outcomes.

pass2.systemImpact: VirtualMachiningDeepLearningEngine (ghost) once built predicts machining-simulation outcomes consumed by the SIMULATE pipeline stage; predictions that diverge from real machining outcomes give operators false confidence at the pre-machine gate.
csDepth: Simulated predictions must be validated against REAL machining outcomes, not against the simulator that generated the training labels — a sim-to-sim loop just learns the simulator's biases.
Virtual-machining simulation feature extraction is high-dimensional spatiotemporal data; choose a representation (voxel grid vs feature summary) that the downstream model can consume without OOM.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MISC-ME.title: Train MetaLearningOptimizerEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

pass1.buildNote: The meta-learning optimizer trains over a task distribution — validate that learned hyperparameters transfer to unseen tasks, not just memorize the training tasks.

pass2.systemImpact: MetaLearningOptimizerEngine is the shared meta-learning substrate referenced by every domain meta-learning unit (lathe, milling, post-processor) — a regression here propagates to all of them. It is the highest-leverage AI-training unit because it is a common dependency.
csDepth: The optimizer learns hyperparameters over a task distribution — validate that learned hyperparameters TRANSFER to unseen tasks, not just minimize loss on the training tasks (the overfit-to-task-set failure mode).
Gradient-based optimizer state (momentum, adaptive LR) must be serialized with the checkpoint so a resumed meta-training run does not silently restart the optimizer from cold.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-POST-CN.title: Train CNCControllerDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: CNCControllerDeepLearningEngine is a ghost engine — build then train on multi-controller G-code; validate dialect classification on held-out programs.

pass2.systemImpact: CNCControllerDeepLearningEngine (ghost) once built classifies controller dialects feeding the post-processor pipeline; a mis-classified dialect routes G-code through the wrong post-processor template, producing NC output the machine rejects. ppDispatcher and the master post-processor consume this.
csDepth: Controller-dialect classification over G/M-code grammar — extract grammar-level features (canned-cycle codes, address-word patterns), not raw text, or the model learns comment-style noise.
Controller families are imbalanced in any real corpus (Fanuc/Haas dominate); class-balance the training set or the model never learns rare dialects.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-POST-PO.title: Train PostProcessorDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: PostProcessorDeepLearningEngine is a ghost engine — build then train; validate generated post-processor logic against rendered NC output.

pass2.systemImpact: PostProcessorDeepLearningEngine (ghost) feeds post-processor logic generation consumed by ppDispatcher and the POST_PROCESS pipeline stage; generated logic must be validated against rendered NC output — a model that produces plausible-but-wrong post logic ships broken NC programs.
csDepth: Validate generated post-processor logic by RENDERING it and parsing the NC output, not by string-similarity to a reference — the post-processor's correctness is in the rendered program, not the template text.
Post-processor template feature extraction must capture the template's control-flow structure (conditionals, blocks), not just token frequency.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-POST-PO.title: Train PostProcessorMetaLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

pass1.buildNote: Partition the post-processor corpus by controller family as distinct tasks — validate fast-adaptation to a new controller held out of meta-training.

pass2.systemImpact: PostProcessorMetaLearningEngine produces fast-adapting post-processor models; its value is adapting to a NEW controller with few examples. The task partition is by controller family — if a held-out controller leaks into meta-training, the fast-adapt claim consumed by ppDispatcher is false.
csDepth: Partition the post-processor corpus by controller family as distinct meta-learning tasks — fast-adaptation must be validated on a controller family entirely held out of meta-training.
A new controller often has very few examples — the inner-loop adaptation must be stable in the few-shot regime; verify it does not diverge with a tiny support set.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-SPEEDFE.title: Train SpeedFeedDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: feature extraction (material ISO group, tool, DOC)
pass1.buildNote: SpeedFeedDeepLearningEngine output must be clamped to the canonical physics envelope — import constants from constants.ts, never inline kc1.1 values.

pass2.systemImpact: SpeedFeedDeepLearningEngine output feeds calcDispatcher speed/feed advisory and the SPEED_FEED pipeline stage across all domains; it is a cross-domain consumer, so a regression affects mill, lathe, and CAM pipelines. Output must be clamped to the canonical physics envelope (constants.ts kc1.1 values).
csDepth: Never inline kc1.1 / Kienzle / Taylor constants — import from constants.ts; the ML output is bounded by physics, and the bound's source of truth must be the canonical file (P=1800, M=2100, K=1100, N=700, S=2800, H=3200).
Feature extraction must key material on the ISO group, not free-text material name — a name-string feature fragments the same material across spelling variants.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-WIRE-EL.title: Train ElectrodeDeepLearningEngine on full pre-revenue corpus (JM-DIE 76K + MIT-OCW + v8.89 MIT kernels)

csKnowledge: supervised training loop with validation split
pass1.buildNote: Train ElectrodeDeepLearningEngine on a held-out validation slice; electrode-design predictions must respect EDM physics constants, not be invented by the model.

pass2.systemImpact: ElectrodeDeepLearningEngine feeds electrode-design recommendations through edmDispatcher consumed by ElectrodeDesignEngine and the WEDM/sinker EDM pipeline; predictions must respect EDM physics constants — a model that invents electrode geometry ships unmachinable electrode designs into APPW-MS8's sinker EDM bridge.
csDepth: Electrode-geometry feature extraction must encode the geometric envelope (overburn, spark gap) as physics-bounded features, not free parameters the model can extrapolate past.
EDM physics ground-truth labelling must come from canonical EDM constants — the WEDM domain has 62 engines; the trained model is an accelerator over that physics, never the authority.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW01.title: Wire AI Core Engines to aiReasoningDispatcher

csKnowledge: Zod schema validation at the MCP boundary
round-trip E2E assertion through the dispatcher
pass1.buildNote: Wiring is incomplete unless the action appears in the z.enum(ACTIONS) gate AND has a real executor body — a ghost-wired enum entry 100% fails in production.

pass2.systemImpact: Wiring AI core engines to aiReasoningDispatcher makes them reachable from the MCP surface; an enum-only ghost-wire 100% fails in production and the stop_on_unwired_assets hook will block the Stop. Every AI-MAX-MS0 and AWARE-MS0 consumer that calls aiReasoningDispatcher actions depends on these wires being real executors.
csDepth: A wiring is incomplete unless the action is BOTH in the z.enum(ACTIONS) gate AND backed by an executor body — the ghost-wired-orphan class (enum entry + slimResponse but no executor) passes naive tests and 100%-fails live.
A MockMCPServer that bypasses the z.enum() SDK gate false-greens a missing-from-enum action — the round-trip E2E must drive the real dispatcher, not a mock.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW02.title: Create Schema Definitions for AI Core Actions

pass1.buildNote: Read the engine's actual input shape before writing the schema — a schema that disagrees with the engine produces a silent runtime mismatch.

pass2.systemImpact: These schema definitions are the contract between the MCP boundary and the AI core engines; a schema that disagrees with the engine's actual input shape produces a silent runtime mismatch that U-AIW01's wiring then routes — schema drift here breaks every consumer downstream.
csDepth: Read the engine's actual input signature before authoring the Zod schema — a schema written from an assumed shape is the recurring schema-blindness bug; the engine source is the source of truth.
A discriminated union schema must have an exhaustive discriminant — a missing variant makes Zod reject a valid payload at runtime, not at type-check time.

csKnowledge: round-trip E2E assertion through the dispatcher
pass1.buildNote: Guard engines must fail closed — a wiring error should default to BLOCK, never silently allow an unsafe operation through.

Attachments must be keyed to a STABLE record id, not an array index — a re-ordered timeline would otherwise orphan attachments; write each event atomically so a crash mid-write does not leave a partial event.

csKnowledge: graceful fail-soft when software is absent
pass1.buildNote: Detect installed CAD software by probing the registry and known install paths — fail soft (return not-installed), never throw, when nothing is found.

pass2.systemImpact: CADInstallationProbeEngine is the first stage of CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0 — every bridge (U-CAUT02..07) and the router (U-CAUT10) keys off which CAD software it reports as installed. If it throws when software is absent rather than returning not-installed, the whole automation dispatcher fails to initialize on a machine missing one CAD package.
csDepth: Windows registry probing must fail soft — a missing registry key is the expected 'not installed' case, not an exception; return a structured not-installed result, never throw (R12 honest, but soft for an expected-absent case).
Registry + filesystem path discovery should cross-check — a registry entry without a resolvable install path means a broken/uninstalled package; report that distinctly from cleanly-absent.

csKnowledge: error handling across the COM boundary
pass1.buildNote: COM access to SolidWorks must release the IDispatch reference and surface COM HRESULT failures loudly — leaked COM objects wedge the app.

pass2.systemImpact: SolidWorksAutomationBridge is the COM access path consumed by CADAutomationRouter (U-CAUT10) for .sldprt/.sldasm/.slddrw files; it sets the COM-lifecycle convention that the Inventor bridge (U-CAUT03) explicitly mirrors. A leaked IDispatch reference wedges the SolidWorks process and accumulates orphans the CADProcessSpawner (U-CAUT08) must reap.
csDepth: COM/IDispatch interop must release every reference deterministically — a leaked COM object keeps the SolidWorks process alive; use a try/finally release pattern, not GC-dependent cleanup.
COM HRESULT failures must be surfaced loudly with the HRESULT code — a swallowed COM error looks like a clean no-op but left a wedged process.

csKnowledge: error handling across the COM boundary
pass1.buildNote: COM access to Inventor must release references and surface HRESULT failures — match the SolidWorks bridge's COM lifecycle convention.

pass2.systemImpact: InventorAutomationBridge is the COM path for .ipt/.iam/.idw consumed by CADAutomationRouter; it must match the SolidWorks bridge's COM lifecycle convention (U-CAUT02) so the router treats both uniformly. csDepth: Match the SolidWorks bridge's COM lifecycle convention — divergent COM cleanup between two bridges makes the router's process management inconsistent and one bridge will leak.
Inventor's .iam assembly model loads referenced .ipt files lazily — the bridge must handle a missing referenced part gracefully, not crash the whole assembly open.

csKnowledge: subprocess spawn of a Python interpreter
stdin/stdout IPC with the FreeCAD process
pass1.buildNote: FreeCAD access spawns a Python subprocess — set a timeout, capture stderr, and kill the orphan if the .FCStd parse hangs.

pass2.systemImpact: FreeCADAutomationBridge spawns a Python subprocess for .FCStd access; it is consumed by CADAutomationRouter and its orphan-Python processes are exactly what CADProcessSpawner (U-CAUT08) and the fleet-reaper must clean up. A hung FreeCAD parse with no timeout accumulates orphans that OOM the host.
csDepth: Subprocess spawn must set a hard timeout and capture stderr — a .FCStd parse that hangs with no timeout leaves an orphan Python process; kill it on timeout, do not wait indefinitely.
stdin/stdout IPC with the FreeCAD process needs a framed protocol (length-prefixed or delimiter) — raw stream parsing can fuse two messages or split one across reads.

pass1.buildNote: Mastercam access goes through a .NET hook — surface .NET exceptions loudly and verify the addin host process exits cleanly.

pass2.systemImpact: MastercamAutomationBridge is the .NET-hook path for .mcx*/.mcam consumed by CADAutomationRouter; Mastercam is the most-used CAM vendor, so this bridge is high-traffic. A .NET exception swallowed at the cross-language boundary looks like a clean failure but left a wedged addin host the fleet-reaper must reap.
csDepth: Surface .NET exceptions across the process boundary loudly — a cross-language IPC boundary swallows exceptions easily; serialize the .NET exception type and message back to the Node caller.
Verify the .NET addin host process exits cleanly after each operation — a host that lingers is an orphan; track its PID with CADProcessSpawner.

csKnowledge: request timeout + retry on connection refused
pass1.buildNote: Fusion 360 access is an HTTP bridge — handle connection-refused (bridge not started), set timeouts, and never assume the local server is up.

pass2.systemImpact: Fusion360AutomationBridge is the HTTP-bridge path for .f3d/.f3z consumed by CADAutomationRouter; the cad-fusion-training-ms0 wiki documents that Fusion cloud is unreachable without Forge creds, so this bridge must degrade gracefully when the local server is down rather than blocking the whole router.
csDepth: Handle connection-refused explicitly — the Fusion HTTP bridge server may not be started; never assume the local server is up, set a request timeout, and report bridge-unavailable distinctly from a parse failure.
An HTTP bridge needs idempotent retry on transient connection errors but NOT on a 4xx — distinguish a not-started server (retry) from a bad request (fail fast).

pass1.buildNote: hyperMILL access uses AC Python — set a timeout, capture stderr, and reap the orphan interpreter if the .hmc operation hangs.

pass2.systemImpact: HyperMILLAutomationBridge is the AC-Python path for .hmc consumed by CADAutomationRouter; like the FreeCAD bridge it spawns an interpreter subprocess whose orphans the CADProcessSpawner and fleet-reaper must reap. hyperMILL has 25 already-extracted assets — the bridge reads existing files, no re-extraction.
csDepth: AC Python automation spawns an interpreter subprocess — set a timeout, capture stderr, and reap the orphan on a hung .hmc operation; match the FreeCAD bridge's subprocess lifecycle convention.
Subprocess timeout handling must distinguish a slow-but-progressing operation from a true hang — a fixed timeout that is too short kills a large legitimate .hmc file.

pass1.buildNote: The process spawner must track every PID and reap orphans on timeout/crash — a leaked CAD process accumulates and OOMs the host.

pass2.systemImpact: CADProcessSpawner is the shared subprocess-lifecycle manager that every CAD bridge (U-CAUT02..07) routes its spawns through; it is the single chokepoint preventing CAD-process orphan accumulation. If it leaks a PID, the fleet-reaper's slot-attribution layer is the only backstop, and a leaked CAD process can OOM the memory-pressured host.
csDepth: Track every spawned PID in a registry and reap on timeout/crash — a leaked CAD process accumulates; this is the same orphan class the fleet-reaper handles, so the spawner should be the first line of defense.
PID tracking has a reuse hazard — the OS recycles PIDs; track spawn time alongside PID so a recycled PID is not mistaken for the original process (the fleet-reaper PID-reuse edge case).

csKnowledge: dependency injection for the bridge layer
hermetic mock that mirrors the real producer shape
pass1.buildNote: The CI mock layer must mirror the REAL bridge response shape — hermetic fakes that fabricate a shape the producer never emits false-green the tests.

pass2.systemImpact: CADAutomationMockLayer provides deterministic fixtures so CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0's CI runs without real CAD software installed; if the mock fabricates a response shape the real bridge never emits, every CI test false-greens and a production bridge bug ships. This is the documented 'hermetic fakes don't prove wiring' hazard.
csDepth: The mock MUST mirror the REAL bridge response shape — record real bridge responses as fixtures; a hand-fabricated shape that diverges from the producer false-greens the tests (the RGS-TOOL-AUTOINVOKE MS0 false-green class).
Dependency injection for the bridge layer lets CI swap the mock in — but the suite must ALSO ship at least one real-bridge E2E (gated on software presence) so the mock-vs-real divergence is caught.

pass1.buildNote: The router selects a bridge by file format — make the format→bridge table explicit and exhaustive; fail loud on an unknown extension.

pass2.systemImpact: CADAutomationRouter is the unified format→bridge selector that CADAutomationDispatcher (U-CAUT11) invokes; it is the single dispatch point over all six bridges. An unhandled file extension that silently no-ops, rather than failing loud, makes the dispatcher return empty for a whole CAD format class.
csDepth: The format→bridge dispatch table (strategy pattern) must be explicit and exhaustive — fail loud on an unknown extension; a default-case that silently returns empty hides an unsupported-format bug.
The router should consult CADInstallationProbeEngine — routing a .sldprt to the SolidWorks bridge is futile if SolidWorks is not installed; surface installed-but-absent distinctly.

csKnowledge: Zod schema validation at the MCP boundary
round-trip E2E assertion through the dispatcher
pass1.buildNote: Each CAD-automation action must be in the z.enum() gate with a real executor — verify the round-trip; an enum-only entry is a ghost.

pass2.systemImpact: CADAutomationDispatcher is the MCP surface for CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0 — it exposes the router (U-CAUT10) and bridges as dispatcher actions; an enum-only ghost-wire makes the whole CAD-automation capability unreachable from the MCP surface and stop_on_unwired_assets blocks the Stop. The 30-file smoke test (U-CAUT12) drives this dispatcher.
csDepth: Each CAD-automation action must be in the z.enum() gate with a real executor — verify the round-trip; an enum-only entry is a ghost that 100%-fails live.
Zod validation at the MCP boundary must match the router's actual input shape — read the router signature before authoring the schema (schema-blindness).

pass1.buildNote: A 30-file multi-format smoke test must drive the real router+bridges — at least one real-file E2E, not only hermetic mocks.

pass2.systemImpact: The 30-file multi-format smoke test is the integration regression oracle for the whole CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0 milestone — it drives the real router + bridges + dispatcher end to end. If it runs only hermetic mocks, a production bridge or router bug ships green; it must include at least one real-file E2E.
csDepth: A smoke test must drive the REAL router + bridges, not only the mock layer — at least one real-file E2E per format, gated on software presence, is the only thing that proves the mock matches the producer.
A 30-file sweep is a fixture-management problem — store fixtures content-addressably and assert concrete per-file results, not just 'no exception thrown' (R9).

pass1.buildNote: Consensus must surface disagreement explicitly — when 2+ models diverge, return the conflict, do not pick silently or average.

pass2.systemImpact: SecondOpinionConsensusEngine is the multi-model disagreement-surfacing layer that other AI-routed CAD/CAM units lean on for high-stakes decisions — its design mirrors the 3-of-3 scrutiny gate doctrine. If it silently picks or averages when models diverge (R7 violation), a confidently-wrong single model overrides a correct dissent and the conflict never reaches a human.
csDepth: Quorum voting needs a tie-breaking and abstention policy — with 2 models a disagreement is a 1-1 tie that MUST escalate, not coin-flip; with N models define whether a non-strict majority counts and whether a low-confidence vote abstains rather than votes.

Disagreement detection on free-text outputs is not exact-equality — use semantic divergence (Jaccard over normalized tokens, or embedding cosine distance) with a calibrated threshold; raw string inequality flags trivial paraphrases as disagreement and floods the human queue.

pass1.buildNote: Headless Creo fixtures must run without GUI — verify each fixture exercises the real automation API, not a stub that returns hardcoded geometry.

pass2.systemImpact: CreoIntegrationTestSuite is the regression net for the Creo CAD bridge — it is what CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0's coverage exit gate (U-CUC18) counts toward the 95%-by-bridge threshold. If its fixtures secretly return hardcoded geometry instead of driving the real Creo automation API, the suite passes green while the Creo bridge is actually broken in production, and the coverage gate certifies a false positive.
csDepth: Headless integration fixtures must be suite-lifetime in setup/teardown — a per-test backup/restore on a real Creo session file is the documented footgun that deleted a live system-viz graph; back up once at suite start, restore once at suite exit.

COM automation mocking is a hermetic-fakes hazard: a mock that bypasses the real COM marshalling proves nothing about production wiring — at least one fixture must drive the actual Creo API end-to-end as a real-data oracle.

pass1.buildNote: CATIA CAA headless fixtures must be suite-lifetime (not per-test) so backup/restore is symmetric — asymmetric per-test teardown is a footgun on real files.

pass2.systemImpact: CATIAIntegrationTestSuite is the regression net for the CATIA bridge and feeds the CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 coverage exit gate (U-CUC18). If its CAA fixtures pass against a fake harness, the coverage gate certifies CATIA support that does not actually work, and CAM/quote pipelines that route CATIA parts fail silently downstream.
csDepth: Suite-lifetime fixture setup/teardown is mandatory on real CAA session files — asymmetric per-test teardown that unlinks then can't restore is the exact bug class that wiped a real fixture file; gate the backup on a once-per-process flag and restore in a beforeExit handler.

CAA automation is process-affine and slow — fixtures should share one CATIA process across the suite (one COM connect/disconnect) rather than spawn per test, but then test isolation must be enforced by explicit document-close between tests or state leaks between cases.

pass1.buildNote: Crash recovery must be idempotent — re-attach + replay can't double-apply commands; checkpoint the command log atomically before each replay.

pass2.systemImpact: CADCrashRecoveryEngine is what keeps a long CAD automation job (e.g. the 20K-file GroundTruthBatchExtractor) survivable across a crash — its watchdog + re-attach + replay is depended on by every long-running CAD bridge operation. If replay double-applies commands, the recovered CAD model diverges from the intended one and silently corrupts whatever pipeline consumes it.
csDepth: Idempotent re-attach requires the command log to carry a monotonic sequence id and the engine to record the last-successfully-applied id atomically before each replay — without it, a crash between 'command applied' and 'log advanced' replays the command and double-applies (an extrude becomes a double-extrude).

Watchdog process supervision must distinguish a wedged-but-alive CAD process from a genuinely dead one — killing a slow-but-progressing process is as harmful as missing a hung one; use a liveness heartbeat plus a progress signal, not PID-existence alone (PID reuse hazard).

pass1.buildNote: Each log entry hashes the prior entry's hash — any gap or mismatch in the chain must fail loud as tamper detection, never be silently skipped.

pass2.systemImpact: CADPluginTamperAuditLogEngine is the tamper-evidence layer for CAD plugin command history — security audits and CADAccessControlRBACABACEngine incident review depend on its hash chain being verifiable. If a chain gap is silently skipped instead of failing loud, tampering becomes undetectable and the audit log's entire security value is void.
csDepth: A hash-chained / Merkle log is append-only by construction — concurrent appenders must be serialized through a single writer or a lock, because two writers each hashing the current tip produce a fork; an append-only .jsonl with one canonical writer is the safer data structure than a mutable JSON file.

Chain verification is O(n) over the whole log — for a long-lived CAD plugin this grows unboundedly; checkpoint the chain (periodic signed Merkle roots) so verification can start from the last trusted root rather than genesis, while keeping any gap a hard fail.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CAD-APP-19.title: MastercamHeadlessIntegrationTestSuite — filling cap-11 gap for #1 app

The suite must drive the real NET-Hook API in at least one E2E fixture — a 'hermetic fakes don't prove wiring' violation here is high-cost because a missing-from-enum dispatcher action passes a mock 100% while production is 100% broken.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC-AI03.title: CADCapabilityNegotiatorEngine — resolves intent vs adapter capability; falls back or fails-fast per policy

csKnowledge: capability set intersection (intent requirements vs adapter feature set)
policy-driven fallback decision tree (fallback vs fail-fast)
pass1.buildNote: Fail-fast path must surface the exact unmet capability (R12) — never silently degrade an unsupported intent; test both fallback and fail-fast policies with real capability gaps.

pass2.systemImpact: The capability negotiator is the gatekeeper between an abstract CAD intent and a concrete vendor adapter (Fusion/Inventor/SolidWorks/hyperCAD-S) — every CAD generation request routed through prism_cad / prism_cadautomation passes through it. If it silently degrades an unsupported intent instead of failing fast, downstream adapters receive an under-specified request and produce wrong geometry that propagates into CAM and the print-to-program pipeline undetected.
csDepth: Capability-set intersection is a subset test, but the result must be a three-valued outcome (fully-supported / partially-supported-with-fallback / unsupported) — collapsing partial-support into a boolean loses the information needed to choose between fallback and fail-fast.

The fallback decision tree is a policy-driven branch; the policy itself must be data, not hardcoded conditionals — otherwise adding a fifth CAD adapter forces an engine edit and a code review instead of a config change.
